title: Live endpoints surface `random.uniform()` / `random.randint()` data as real values
description: Multiple service methods that are wired to authenticated production endpoints return Python-`random` simulated values with no flag indicating mock data: `admin_service.get_system_health_data()` (CPU/mem/error rate), `admin_service.list_users()` (entire user list), `recommendation_service.run_backtest()` (entire backtest result), `recommendation_service.generate_performance_records()` (recommendation P&L), `recommendation_service.generate_alert_history()`, `portfolio_rebalancing.generate_performance_data_points()` (portfolio chart values), `socketio_service._stream_price_updates()` (live price feed broadcast to subscribers). For a SEC-regulated investment platform this is both a correctness bug and a compliance risk: the platform's own SEC disclosure (`recommendation_service.py:25-31`) warns about data freshness yet here it ships entirely fabricated values without any `mock=True` flag.
recommendation: Tag every fake-data method with a `_DEMO_DATA = True` constant or wrap with a feature flag (`if not settings.DEMO_MODE: raise NotImplementedError`); ensure the response includes `"data_source": "simulated"`. Better: replace with real implementations where feasible (cleanup_old_data tasks already populate metrics; system metrics already collected by `monitoring`/`metrics` endpoints). At minimum, audit each call site and either implement or block with `HTTP 501 Not Implemented`.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -nE "random\.(uniform | randint | choice)" backend/services/*.py` returns 0 hits in production code paths; demo-only code is gated behind `settings.DEMO_MODE`. Integration test on `/api/admin/system/health` returns `psutil`-based real numbers, not `random.uniform(20, 80)`.

title: Two competing real-time push transports (raw WebSocket + Socket.IO)
description: `websocket_service.py::EnhancedConnectionManager` (active per scope-01 audit; `EnhancedConnectionManager` imported by `backend/api/routers/websocket.py:25-32`). `socketio_service.py::sio` is a Socket.IO `AsyncServer` instance with its own subscription model. Both broadcast price updates with mock data; clients must choose one. Dual code path with no integration plan.
recommendation: Pick one. Socket.IO is friendlier for browsers behind proxies; raw WebSocket has lower overhead. Document the choice in `docs/architecture/` and delete the other. The `_stream_price_updates` random-data emitter in socketio_service exists in BOTH transports (F-02-003) — fixing one without the other still ships fake data.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: only one transport is registered in `main.py`; frontend WebSocket client code points to one URL.

title: Fallback risk metrics return hardcoded plausible-but-fake values
description: When `prices` is short or empty, returns `{"beta": 1.15, "alpha": 0.02, "sharpe_ratio": 1.85, ...}`. These look like real risk metrics. A caller that doesn't check `len(prices) >= 30` upstream will surface them to the user as "risk metrics for [TICKER] with no data". Same problem as F-02-003 (silent fake data).
recommendation: Return `{}` or raise `InsufficientDataError`. Caller should explicitly handle the missing-data case.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `if prices and len(prices) >= 30` short-path returns real metrics; else raises explicit exception.

title: Trained model binaries absent — platform runs on dummy fallbacks
description: `ml_models/` contains only JSON config/result files. No `xgboost_model.pkl`, `lstm_weights.pth`, or Prophet `.pkl` files exist. `model_manager.py:199-211` silently substitutes `DummyLSTM`, `DummyXGBoost`, `DummyProphet` that return random values. All ML-driven recommendations in production are random-based, not model-based.
recommendation: Run full training pipeline to produce and store model binaries, or download from HF Hub (`HF_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true`). Add startup health gate that fails fast if all models are in fallback state.

title: Feature drift monitoring and statistics use mock random data
description: `monitor_feature_drift()` at line 666 reads: `"Mock data for demonstration - in real implementation, query feature store"` and generates `np.random.normal(0,1,1000)`. `get_feature_statistics()` at line 743 returns `np.random.randint(1000, 10000)` for counts and other random values. Drift alerts will fire randomly regardless of actual data distribution.
recommendation: Implement real feature store persistence using the SQLAlchemy `db_engine` already initialized in `__init__`. Query actual feature values from DB or time-series storage for drift calculation.
acceptance_test_hint: `monitor_feature_drift("rsi_14d")` returns a `FeatureDriftMetrics` whose `drift_score` changes with actual data, not randomly
